title: GaussCast: Dependency-Aware Shared Block Retrieval for Multi-User Layered 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Layered 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables progressive novel-view synthe- sis, but large scenes such as city models remain gigabytes in size even after state-of-the-art compression, making full pre-download impractical under band- width limits or sub-second startup targets. Progressive delivery transmits content incrementally according to viewing demand, but existing systems plan it for each user independently. When several users explore the same scene concur- rently, as in virtual tours or XR classrooms, their viewpoints differ yet depend on the same lower-layer blocks, so per-user delivery fetches the same prerequi- sites from the origin once per user, duplicating shared upstream traffic. Edge caches and request aggregation remove part of this duplication, but they act only after requests exist: they neither plan which blocks a group should fetch jointly nor respect rendering dependencies, so a refinement block can arrive before its required lower layers and remain unusable. We present GaussCast, a dependency-aware delivery framework that structures layered 3DGS scenes as versioned cell–layer–chunk retrieval blocks with explicit dependency meta- data. An edge proxy aggregates short-horizon user demand, fetches a shared base of widely needed prerequisite blocks once upstream, and spends the remain- ing budget on per-user supplements; admission enforces dependency closure under per-window byte budgets and user rendering deadlines. We implement GaussCast over Information-Centric Networking and describe mappings to HTTP/CDN and relay deployments. In trace-driven evaluation with multi-user sessions derived from real 6DoF navigation traces, GaussCast reduces shared edge-to-origin upstream traffic by 26% and time-to-first-frame by 27%, and improves viewport quality and fairness over per-user baselines, with gains grow- ing as cross-user overlap increases. Implementation and evaluation artifacts are publicly available at https://github.com/ulen2000/gausscast-sim.
